new_statements.quote: When closed syllable monosyllabic roots are lengthened, the roots takes on an additional, weak "echo vowel", a weak version of the vowel in the first syllable. This happens because the first syllable of roots in Ngiemboon is always stressed, the second syllable and any suffix is always unstressed. Here is an example: PERFECTIVE [fàʔ] IMPERFECTIVE [fàʔà] "to work"

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngiemboon is a tone language (four noun-stem melodies, H/L on verb roots, heavy tonal perturbation). Independently of tone, stress is fixed on the first syllable of the root; the root's second syllable and any suffix (-te or an echo vowel) are always unstressed. Since roots are mostly monosyllabic and prefixes (vowel or syllabic nasal) precede the root, this amounts to root-initial stress rather than word-initial stress in the strict sense.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the claim is made in passing to explain why lengthening of closed-syllable roots yields a weak echo vowel rather than a full vowel.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the root/stem (prefix + root + suffix word); statement is made for lexical roots, illustrated with verb citation forms (perfective vs imperfective). No instrumental evidence; not the focus of the sketch, which otherwise treats tone as the prosodic system that is written.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Ngiemboon (Ngyemboon-Bamileke, nnh, ngie1241) as spoken in the Batcham/Bamougoum area of the West Region, Cameroon, without dialect specification; the same variety underlies the Lonfo & Anderson 2014 dictionary and the PHOIBLE inventory 1628. Bibliographic discrepancy to note: Glottolog files Anderson 1983 as a UCLA dissertation, while Anderson 2008 and Kamdem 2020 cite it as University of Southern California.

sources.note: p. 5 §4.4 'Echo vowels': the first syllable of roots is always stressed; the second syllable and any suffix is always unstressed (explains echo-vowel weakening). Tone (§6) is lexical, four noun-stem melodies, H/L on verbs; no other stress discussion.
